persona: You are a licensed ham (Technician class) who just joined a local ham radio club in person at their weekly meeting -- the club secretary told you 'we're on hams.com, go set yourself up.' You are comfortable with computers and smartphones but this is your first time on this specific site. You want to actually find and join your club online, see who else is in it, and understand what being a club member gets you here (like whether you can use a club-owned radio remotely, or see club-only announcements/events).
legs: Find your club on hams.com and figure out how to actually join it or link your account to it. Is it obvious how, or do you have to guess?

Once you're associated with a club (or if you can't find a way to actually join one), explore what club membership is supposed to unlock -- a member roster, club-only content, shared equipment, anything club-specific. Is it clear what you get?
See if there's a way to use or reserve a club-owned radio/station remotely, since your club secretary mentioned this is possible. Is that findable and does it make sense?

Look for any club officer or leadership-only features (even though you're not an officer) -- would you be able to tell if your club had an officer, and is there any indication of who to contact if you have questions?
